Subject: RE: MAP draft + integration milestone proposal (technical notes / questions)

Hi all —

Quick technical notes ahead of the kickoff. I’ll be on the call 2026-03-02 and can walk through these items live, but wanted to surface them so Daniel has context.

1) SDK integration (client-side)
- Redwood provides a JS + Python SDK. The SDK handles token refresh and KV cache priming. For a browser-based client we recommend using our streaming WebSocket client to reduce round trips. If you’re embedding in a server-side app we can use HTTP streaming.
- Sample code and a runnable sample app are attached in the SDK PDF.

2) Streaming: WebSocket vs SSE
- WebSocket: bi-directional, better for low-latency interactive UIs and tool-calls. Requires an allowlisted origin or a proxy if you host behind strict CORS policies.
- SSE (server-sent events): simpler and works over plain HTTP, but no client->server messages except via separate channels; good if you only need one-way tokenized streaming.
- Recommendation: NimbleHealth UI looks interactive per the demo — recommend WebSocket for the initial build. Owner: Daniel Kim (Nimble) for client choice; Redwood (Aditya) will provide example impl and QA plan.

3) Tool calling + structured outputs
- We support JSON-schema-validated structured outputs and an extensible tool-calling interface. For EHR lookup the recommended approach: define a small tool schema (input: patient_id, fields[], auth_token) and test it in staging with mock responses.
- Auth: we support API-key and OAuth-style token exchange. For server-to-server EHR calls we usually recommend a short-lived token flow (recommended) but API-key is supported for initial proofs of concept.

4) Security & networking
- For Dedicated or Private deployments we’ll provide IP ranges and TLS requirements. For hosted API usage, allowlist the outbound IPs documented in the attached Data Security Profile. Stephanie — if you can provide the exact allowlist format NimbleHealth uses (CIDR or hostnames) we’ll include it in the MAP.

5) Test/validation harness
- We’ll provide a prompt set and a small regression harness (pytest-based) that runs against staging and checks structured output validity + latency targets.

Action items before kickoff:
- Daniel: confirm preferred streaming protocol (WebSocket vs SSE) and provide staging EHR endpoint + sample response shape.
- Emily: confirm sprint boundary date so we can align SDK deliverable (you mentioned 2026-03-25).
- Stephanie (Redwood): please prepare the security checklist to share post-kickoff.

Thanks — I’ll prepare the demo slides and a short checklist to run through on the kickoff call.

—Aditya
